headline: High: Prefect can fetch GitHub APIs while the content-writing agent has broad egress, creating default data-exfiltration and workflow-conflict risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared filesystem or direct message channel is documented, so prompt injection is not default. However, Prefect can call GitHub APIs and the content-writing agent has broad network egress, so if outputs are manually bridged or copied into workflows, attacker-controlled content could be reinterpreted. The pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF outputs from agent_a are copied into agent_b workflow inputs without sanitization
IF agent_b ingests remote API content as trusted instructions
mitigations: Use a copy-paste checklist to strip instructions from agent_a outputs
Add a one-line provenance note before passing text to agent_b
Disable any auto-ingest of API responses into prompts
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent_a has broad network egress and agent_b also has broad egress plus API access, so any shared workspace or copied artifacts could flow outward. Agent_b touches workflow metadata, which is not highly sensitive by itself, but the pair can still leak operational context through outbound requests. The interaction is plausible in default use, though not proven by a shared filesystem.
conditions: IF either agent receives sensitive workflow metadata in its prompt or files
IF copied artifacts from one agent are sent through the other's outbound requests
mitigations: Review prompts for secrets before handoff
Keep sensitive files out of shared folders
Use separate API tokens for each agent
Turn off outbound calls during sensitive runs
requires-engineering: isolate workspaces per agent

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and agent_b can call external APIs, so overlapping writes to shared remote resources are plausible if they are pointed at the same project or repo. No locking or coordination primitive is documented for either agent, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low. The conflict is about shared mutable resources, not local filesystem writes.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to modify the same remote resource or repository
IF changes are made without an external lock or review step
mitigations: Assign one agent read-only access
Use separate branches or work queues
Add a manual approval step before writes
Check for concurrent runs before starting
requires-engineering: implement resource locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent_b can act on workflow metadata and external API results, so if it treats agent_a's written content as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream orchestration. Agent_a is a content-writing agent, which makes it a plausible source of unverified facts or instructions. Because no verification step is documented, the pair has a default inference chain rather than a blocked one.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as an input artifact without verification
IF downstream automation is triggered from that unverified content
mitigations: Require a human review before execution
Add a validation checklist for agent_a outputs
Limit agent_b to read-only dry runs
Log source provenance for each handoff
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, so compliance risk is limited to general uncertainty. Agent_b handles workflow metadata and agent_a is a content-writing tool with broad egress, but there is no evidence of regulated data classes or cross-border restrictions. I cite both profiles because the pairwise deployment context is what matters here.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent's inputs
IF deployment policy requires residency or retention guarantees not present here
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in prompts
Confirm retention settings before use
Document the data classes each agent may see
Use separate environments for regulated workloads
